info.bio:
Team Dresch is an American punk rock band from Portland, Oregon, formed in 1993. Originally from Olympia, Washington, they made a significant impression on the queercore movement, as well as on the riot grrrl scene, before breaking up in 1998 and reforming in 2004.

The line up of the group for their first album was Kaia Wilson, vocals and guitar; Jody Bleyle, guitar, bass, and vocals; Donna Dresch, bass and guitar; and Marcéo Martinez on drums.

scenes.name: Foxcore y riot grrrls
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El hardcore había sido un fenómeno masculino; el movimiento «riot grrrl» introduce el «factor chica» en la ecuación de frustración, depresión, desesperación y rabia. Nace en Olympia (fanzines como «Girl Germs», el lema «Revolution Girl Style Now!») y bebe de las cantautoras neoyorquinas, las bandas femeninas californianas (Runaways, Frightwig, L7) y las británicas (Raincoats, Slits). Un movimiento fundado en las letras, no en la música: Mecca Normal, Bikini Kill de Kathleen Hanna (y luego Le Tigre), Bratmobile, Team Dresch, Hole de Courtney Love, Seven Year Bitch, Sleater-Kinney. En California, Mudwimin, 4 Non Blondes, Tribe 8, Tiger Trap, Donnas, Red Aunts, That Dog, Muffs; en el Medio Oeste, Babes In Toyland (Fontanelle, «un arte de emociones extremas») y Sugarsmack; Free Kitten y Luscious Jackson en Nueva York.

podcast.title: Critically Praised and Influential
podcast.body: Team Dresch was part of the riot grrrl scene, which, though not commercially successful, garnered critical praise and was highly influential for subsequent generations of bands. "There were groups like Team Dresh."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Prominent Riot Grrrl Band
podcast.body: Team Dresch is identified as one of the biggest bands in the Riot Grrrl movement, particularly from the Pacific Northwest. "The biggest of the bunch were probably Team Dresh and Sleeter Kinney, both from the Pacific Northwest."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Reunion
podcast.body: Team Dresch has reunited, similar to Sleater-Kinney, showcasing the ongoing influence and activity of bands from the Riot Grrrl and post-Riot Grrrl scenes. "There have been reunions by Sleeter Kinney and Team Dresh"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Semi-Solo Post-Riot Grrrl Supergroup
podcast.body: Team Dresch was described as a "semi-solo post-Riot Grrrl supergroup" centered around Donna Dresch. The band continued the mission of the Riot Grrrl movement into a second wave of groups, maintaining its political and feminist edge. "Another group around at the same time, Slater Kinney was Team Dresh. This was a semi-soda post-Ryade girl supergroup built around Donna Dresh."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Brief Stints with Grunge and Indie Bands
xref.body: For a period, Donna Dresch played with "the guys," including a stint as a member of the Seattle grunge band Screaming Trees and touring Australia playing bass for Dinosaur Jr. These experiences highlight her diverse musical background before forming Team Dresch. "Donna was a member of Seattle Grunge Ben Screaming Trees for a bit and toured Australia playing bass for dinosaur junior."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Traveling Folk Singer
xref.body: Frank is a "fellow traveling folk singer from California" who is the subject of the Team Dresch song "Uncle Frank" from their 1996 album. This song provides a glimpse into the diverse subjects and influences within the post-Riot Grrrl scene. "It's a song about Frank, a fellow traveling folk singer from California, and it's called Uncle Frank."
